children: Petronas Chemicals' absence of scheduled turnarounds and resilient product prices should support a sequential earnings recovery in 4Q, but persistent industry oversupply will limit its gains, AmInvestment Bank analyst Aimi Nasuha Md Nazri says in a note. Higher plant utilization as well as resilient fertilizer and methanol fundamentals are unlikely to fully offset pressure on olefins & derivatives spreads amid substantial global capacity additions, she says. The analyst expects its unit Pengerang Petrochemical business to remain loss-making beyond its 1H 2027 turnaround, as weaker product prices threaten the sustainability of its recent EBITDA recovery. AmInvestment Bank downgrades Petronas Chemicals' rating to sell from hold after its disappointing 9-months earnings, and cuts target price to 3.10 ringgit from 4.80 ringgit. Shares are 2.9% lower at 3.69 ringgit. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
